notes: Summary: evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency fintech customer-facing assistants and real-time reranking; main ask = clear, measurable latency SLOs and predictable reserved GPU planning
Primary constraints: strict regulatory data residency, must run in VPC or on-prem; legal requires p99 SLA tied to client-observed latency (external), not only server-side telemetry
SLO alignment discussion: customer insists on client-side (end-to-end) measurement vs Redwood recommendation to use server-side ingress->egress and documented network delta

Key definitions proposed by Redwood (recommended): p50/p95/p99 calculated on server completion time (server egress final-token timestamp) with explicit mapping to client-observed via monitored delta window; streaming SLOs split into "first-byte" and "final-token" timings

Measurement specifics captured in POC: sample window = 1 minute, aggregation = request-level latencies measured at server egress, include tokenization and decode time but exclude client-side network jitter; customer asked for alternative baseline where edge RTT is included (client-observed), we provided calibration script

Streaming vs non-streaming: non-streaming SLOs measured as time-to-final-token; streaming SLOs defined as two metrics: time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and completion tail (time between first-byte and final-token). recommendation: SLO for streaming 'first-byte p95 < 150ms' and 'final-token p99 < 800ms' for their target model sizes, but exact numbers to be tuned during POC

Client-side timing caveats: browsers vs server SDKs show different RTT variance; suggested approach: dual-reporting in SLA — server-side official SLO + optional client-observed reconciliation for disputes

Cache / warm state assumptions: reserved GPU sizing and SLOs assume warm KV cache (prefix cache hit rate >= 75%); cold-start paths (model load, cache miss) excluded from standard SLO or captured as separate 'cold-start' metric

Throughput guarantees: planning model = tokens/sec per GPU * concurrency; we provided baseline: A100-class equivalent capacity -> ~2500 tokens/sec steady for their quantized model under continuous batching, expecting p95 within target at 600 QPS of short request workloads, but need to validate with their prompt distributions
Reserved GPU planning: suggested commit = capacity to support 3x their 95th percentile QPS to allow headroom for spikes and rolling upgrades; burst pool recommended for peak trading windows

SLA negotiation points flagged: whether p99 is measured over rolling 30-day window vs calendar month, how credits calculate (absolute vs percentage of requests), inclusion/exclusion of force majeure/network outages, precise measurement point (client e2e vs server egress), and minimum sample counts for percentile validity

POC artifacts provided: latency probes, client-side calibration script, synthetic streaming harness, throughput load templates (drive:/deals/sentrypace/pricing-deck-v2.pdf referenced), initial p95/p99 numbers from POC cluster included above
Customer quote (notes): 'We need guarantees that reflect what our users feel — not just nice numbers from the server. If p99 is bad, we lose conversions instantly.'
